title: The Empress Rizia — “No Fault But That She Was a Woman”
summary: Delhi, 1236. When Sultan Iltutmish looked at his sons — given up, in his words, to 'wine, women, gaming, and the worship of the wind' — he trained his eldest daughter Rizia in government instead, and left her as regent when he campaigned. After his death and a brother's six-month collapse, the nobles raised Rizia to the throne. She assumed the imperial robes, gave public audience daily, restored her father's laws and, the chronicler says, distributed justice 'with an equal hand'. When a coalition of provincial governors marched on Delhi, she beat them without a battle — sowing dissension among them until the alliance dissolved, then hunting down the ringleaders. Her undoing was favoritism: she raised Eacoot, an Abyssinian former slave, to Captain General over the Turkish nobles' fury. The governor of Tiberhind rebelled; on the march her own Turkish Omrahs mutinied, killed her general and seized her. In captivity her jailer Altunia married her, and together they raised an army of Gickers and Jits and twice marched on Delhi to win back her empire. Defeated both times by Balin, she and her husband were overtaken in flight and 'inhumanly put to immediate death'. Ferishta's verdict: 'Thus died the Empress Rizia, deserving a better fate.'
why: She was the first and only woman to rule the Delhi Sultanate in her own right — and the book's famous line about her ('the strictest scrutineers of her actions could find in her no fault but that she was a woman') is one of the great backhanded verdicts in historical writing. Her story has everything: a father's gamble, a bluff called without battle, a fatal favorite, a marriage in a prison cell, and two last desperate campaigns.

panels.scene: Delhi, 1236. The emperor Ferose Shaw sits abandoned as his nobles desert with their troops.

dialogue.speaker: Deserting Omrah
dialogue.text: This reign is over. Delhi needs a sovereign worth the name.

panels.caption: Six months and twenty-eight days into his reign, the emperor's own nobles ride for Delhi to raise his sister Rizia to the throne.

panels.scene: Flashback: Sultan Iltutmish's court, years earlier. The aging Sultan defends his choice of regent.

dialogue.speaker: Omrah
dialogue.text: Why your daughter, when you have so many sons?

dialogue.speaker: Iltutmish
dialogue.text: My sons worship the wind. Rizia has a man's head and heart — she is better than twenty such sons.

panels.caption: Her father had seen it early: he trained her in statecraft and made her regent while he campaigned.

panels.scene: Rizia enthroned in imperial robes, petitioners before her.

dialogue.speaker: Rizia
dialogue.text: My father's laws stand. Let every suit be heard.

panels.caption: She casts off the veil, assumes the imperial robes and gives public audience daily — 'the strictest scrutineers could find no fault in her but that she was a woman.'

panels.scene: Night. Rebel governors' camp outside Delhi; suspicion spreading between tents as letters pass hand to hand.

dialogue.speaker: Rizia (writing)
dialogue.text: Suspicion is a better general than any I could send.

panels.caption: Facing a coalition of governors, she sows dissension among them — the alliance melts away without a battle, and the ringleaders are run down.

panels.scene: A court ceremony: Eacoot, the Abyssinian, robed as Captain General; Turkish nobles glower.

dialogue.speaker: Turkish noble
dialogue.text: A slave raised above us all!

panels.caption: Her fatal favor: Eacoot, once a slave, becomes Master of Horse, then Captain General of the Empire.

panels.scene: The march to Tiberhind, midnight: mutiny in the camp, Eacoot cut down, Rizia seized.

dialogue.speaker: Mutineer
dialogue.text: The favorite is dead. Seize the Empress!

panels.caption: Halfway to Tiberhind her own Turkish Omrahs mutiny — her general is killed and she is sent prisoner to the fort.

panels.scene: Inside the fort of Tiberhind: Altunia, her jailer, kneels before her.
panels.caption: The jailer marries his prisoner. Together they raise an army of Gickers and Jits to win back the empire.

panels.scene: Dusty plain near Delhi: two armies collide, Rizia's banner falling back.

dialogue.speaker: Rizia
dialogue.text: Once more. We try once more.

panels.caption: Twice she marches on Delhi; twice Balin defeats her — the troops of Hindostan no match for the horse of Turkestan.

panels.scene: The field of Keitel, 1240: riders overtaking two fugitives.
panels.caption: Taken in the pursuit, Rizia and her husband are put to death. 'Thus died the Empress Rizia, deserving a better fate' — a reign of three years, six months, and six days.

hook: The only woman ever to rule the Delhi Sultanate in her own right — a three-year reign that ended, Ferishta says, 'deserving a better fate.'
